corrected_answer:
STANCE 81 - Account for the defect per tenant on shared serving capacity: redundant calls from one tenant are a noisy-neighbour tax paid by every other tenant in the same pool.

Mechanism. On a shared cluster the prefill pool is a common resource with no per-tenant partition by default. A tenant whose traffic carries a high redundant-call rate lengthens its own prompts and consumes admission slots and KV blocks that would otherwise serve co-resident tenants. The harm therefore appears in the latency of tenants that did not cause it, which is why a fleet-average unnecessary-call rate cannot locate either the cause or the victim.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: redundant calls are concentrated such that the top decile of tenants by redundant-call rate accounts for a disproportionate share of prefill GPU-seconds relative to its share of requests. Falsified if redundant-call rate is uniform across tenants within the noise band, which would mean per-tenant accounting adds no targeting information and a fleet-level fix is appropriate.

Metrics. Per-tenant redundant-call rate, per-tenant share of prefill GPU-seconds and admitted requests, co-resident p95 latency broken out by whether a high-rate tenant is active, KV block occupancy per tenant, plus the standard behavioral set of tool success, tool-required-stratum accuracy, trajectory length, tool latency and recovery rate. All GPU-second splits are ESTIMATE unless read from per-tenant accounting counters; if derived, state the derivation as measured tenant prefill tokens divided by measured pool throughput on the same GPU class.

Controlled experiment. Replay a logged window with tenant identity preserved and compare co-resident p95 latency in blocks where a high-rate tenant is present against matched blocks where it is absent, randomising block assignment rather than comparing consecutive periods. Then apply a per-tenant call quota to the high-rate tenant only and measure the change in co-resident latency, holding pool size, admission policy and request rate fixed.

Confounders. Tenants differ in prompt length and task mix independently of redundancy, so a latency difference can be a workload difference rather than a redundancy effect; matching on prompt-length distribution is required. Prefix cache warmth is tenant-correlated, since repeated tenant traffic warms its own prefixes. Autoscaling triggered mid-window converts the measurement into a control-loop observation.

Rollback criteria. Remove the per-tenant quota immediately if the quotaed tenant's tool-required-stratum accuracy or recovery rate falls below the pre-declared floor, since throttling a tenant to protect others is a fairness change that must not be paid for with correctness. The quota must be a single per-tenant parameter with its value logged per request, and the revert must be exercised in staging before any production application.
risks: Source answer reports fleet-level metrics that cannot locate either the causing tenant or the affected tenant on shared capacity.
Tenants differ in prompt length and task mix, so a co-resident latency difference may be a workload difference rather than a redundancy effect.
Throttling one tenant to protect others is a fairness change that can be silently paid for with that tenant's correctness.
evidence_required: Per-tenant redundant-call rate, prefill GPU-seconds and KV block occupancy read from per-tenant accounting counters.
Randomised present/absent block comparison of co-resident p95 latency with prompt-length distribution matched and pool size, admission policy and request rate held fixed.

STANCE 82 - Check for train/serve skew in how a tool result is rendered: if the serving template differs from the training template, the decision is being made on a distribution the policy never saw.

Mechanism. The tool observation reaching the policy at serving time is produced by the serving template, while the disposition to call or abstain was learned against whatever rendering appeared in the training data. If the two differ in field order, whitespace, key names, truncation or the presence of a call identifier, the tokens that carry the already-known answer differ from the ones the policy learned to condition on. The result is a behavioural defect that no amount of threshold tuning fixes, because the input representation is wrong.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: rendering a logged tool observation through the training template and through the serving template produces token sequences that differ at the observation span, and re-rendering to the training form reduces the unnecessary-call rate by more than the replay noise band. Falsified if the two renderings are token-identical at the observation span, which eliminates skew as an explanation and redirects effort to the policy itself.

Metrics. Token-level diff rate between training-template and serving-template renderings of the same observation, unnecessary-call rate under each rendering, tool success, tool-required-stratum accuracy, trajectory length, tool p95 latency and recovery rate. Report the training template hash and the serving template hash alongside every rate, since a rate without both hashes cannot be reproduced.

Controlled experiment. Take a fixed set of logged trajectories, render each observation under both templates, and compare the tokenised spans directly; this step needs no model inference and is a MEASURED artifact. Then run a two-arm replay on one frozen checkpoint that differs only in the observation rendering, with identical seeds, decode configuration and window, and read the unnecessary-call difference against a control-versus-control noise band.

Confounders. Changing the rendering also changes prompt length, which shifts prefix cache hit rate and token budget at the same time, so a length-matched control rendering is required to separate the two. Tokenizer version differences produce spurious diffs that are not skew. Some trajectories were themselves generated under a third historical template, so the training-template baseline must be pinned to a declared version rather than assumed.

Rollback criteria. Revert the rendering change if tool-required-stratum accuracy or recovery rate degrades, since aligning the template is a serving-path change that touches every request. Retain the prior template as a runnable artifact keyed by hash so the revert is exact, and require that any future template refactor re-run the token-diff check as a blocking step.
risks: Source answer assumes the observation the policy sees at serving time matches the rendering it was trained against.
A rendering change shifts prompt length and prefix cache behaviour at the same time as the intended semantic change.
Tokenizer version differences produce spurious span diffs that are not train/serve skew.
evidence_required: Token-level diff of the same logged observation rendered under the pinned training template and the serving template, with both hashes recorded.
Two-arm replay on one frozen checkpoint differing only in observation rendering, with a length-matched control rendering and a control-versus-control noise band.

STANCE 83 - State that the analysable population is not the production population: privacy redaction and retention limits remove exactly the trajectories most likely to be adjudicable.

Mechanism. Deciding whether an answer was already known requires reading the tool arguments and the prior observation. Those fields are the ones most likely to contain customer data, so they are redacted, hashed or dropped under retention policy, and short retention windows delete older trajectories entirely. The trajectories that survive into the analysis set are therefore selected on a property correlated with the outcome being measured, and the resulting rate is a statement about the surviving subset rather than about production.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: the unnecessary-call rate computed over adjudicable trajectories differs from the rate over all trajectories by more than the replay noise band, once non-adjudicable trajectories are bounded by best-case and worst-case imputation. Falsified if the bounds are tight enough that both extremes fall inside the noise band, which would mean the selection is benign for this metric.

Metrics. Adjudicable fraction of trajectories with the reason for exclusion, unnecessary-call rate over the adjudicable subset, best-case and worst-case bounds under imputation over the excluded set, retention window length, redaction rate by field, and the standard behavioural set of tool success, tool-required-stratum accuracy, trajectory length, tool latency and recovery rate. Any single headline rate quoted without the adjudicable fraction is an ESTIMATE of unknown selection bias.

Controlled experiment. Partition a logged window into adjudicable and non-adjudicable strata using the redaction and retention rules as they stood at collection time, compute the rate on the adjudicable stratum, and then compute the two extreme imputations over the excluded stratum to bound the production rate. Where a privacy-preserving derived feature exists, for example a salted hash of the canonicalised argument tuple, check whether it recovers enough signal to shrink the bounds without exposing raw values.

Confounders. Redaction rules change over time, so the adjudicable fraction is itself a time series and pooling across rule versions mixes populations. Long-running or failing trajectories are more likely to be truncated by retention, which correlates with recovery behaviour. Salted hashes rotate, so cross-window matching on hashed arguments silently fails after rotation.

Rollback criteria. This is an analysis gate rather than a deployment: block any production-wide claim whose imputation bounds do not exclude the decision threshold, and restate the result as scoped to the adjudicable subset. No change to redaction or retention may be made to widen the analysis population without a separate approved privacy review, and no raw argument value may be copied into an analysis store.
risks: Source answer computes a rate without stating that redaction and retention remove trajectories non-randomly.
The excluded trajectories are selected on the very fields required for adjudication, so the surviving subset is biased.
Redaction rules change over time, so pooling across rule versions mixes different populations.
evidence_required: Adjudicable fraction with per-field redaction rate and retention window, reported alongside every rate.
Best-case and worst-case imputation bounds over the excluded stratum, computed under the redaction rules in force at collection time.

STANCE 84 - Justify the study itself: if the adjudication pipeline costs more than the defect, the correct engineering decision is to stop measuring and accept the waste.

Mechanism. Every proposal here carries its own cost in GPU time for replay, human hours for adjudication and engineering time for harness maintenance. The defect it addresses has a bounded cost that can be estimated from logs before any of that is spent. When the expected value of the information is smaller than the cost of obtaining it, running the study is a net loss even if the study is methodologically perfect, and the discipline of computing that comparison first is what separates engineering from activity.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: the upper bound on annual savings from eliminating all redundant calls, computed by an oracle strip over existing logs, is smaller than the fully loaded cost of the proposed adjudication and experimentation programme. Falsified if the oracle-strip bound exceeds the programme cost by a clear margin, which licenses the full programme without further justification.

Metrics. Oracle-strip upper bound on removable tokens and GPU-seconds, converted to currency at the recorded internal rate; adjudication cost per labelled item; replay GPU-seconds per arm; engineering hours per experiment; and the resulting expected value of information. The oracle-strip bound is MEASURED from logs, since it requires no inference; the programme cost and the currency conversion are ESTIMATE and must carry their derivations.

Controlled experiment. Compute the oracle strip first, by removing provably redundant steps from logged trajectories and re-accounting the token and GPU-second totals without running the model. This bounds the achievable win from above only, because a real intervention cannot exceed perfect suppression. Then price the programme from a small pilot: label a modest sample, record actual adjudication throughput, and extrapolate rather than assuming a rate.

Confounders. Oracle stripping assumes downstream behaviour is unchanged after removal, which overstates the win where a removed call would have altered later steps. Internal cost rates are allocations rather than marginal costs, so a saving on paper may free no capacity. Pilot adjudication throughput is optimistic because pilots use the most engaged labellers.

Rollback criteria. If the oracle-strip bound falls below the pre-declared materiality bar, record a no-action decision with the bound and its derivation, and stop; reopening requires new evidence that the bound has moved, not a repeat of the same argument. If a programme was already funded on an unstated bound, halt it and recompute the bound before continuing.
risks: Source answer prescribes an extensive measurement programme without bounding the value of the information it would produce.
Oracle stripping assumes downstream behaviour is unchanged after removal, which overstates the achievable win.
Internal cost rates are allocations rather than marginal costs, so a paper saving may free no real capacity.
evidence_required: Oracle-strip upper bound on removable tokens and GPU-seconds computed from logs without model inference.
Pilot-measured adjudication throughput and replay GPU-seconds per arm, with the currency conversion rate and its derivation recorded.

corrected_answer:
STANCE 85 - Fix the tool response contract before the policy: a result returned without units, precision or an exactness flag gives the policy a rational reason to call again.

Mechanism. A bare numeric result carries no statement of what it means. The policy cannot tell whether the value is rounded, whether it is exact, what unit it is in, or whether it answers the question that was asked. Calling again with different phrasing is a reasonable response to that ambiguity. Treating this as a policy defect misattributes an interface problem to the model, and every downstream intervention then fights a symptom.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: enriching the tool response with an explicit unit, a declared precision and an exactness flag reduces the unnecessary-call rate by more than the replay noise band, without changing the tool's numeric values. Falsified if the enriched contract leaves the rate unchanged, which would show the policy was not conditioning on result ambiguity and would redirect effort to the decision policy.

Metrics. Unnecessary-call rate under the bare and enriched contracts, rate of repeated calls whose arguments differ only in phrasing, tool success, tool-required-stratum accuracy, trajectory length, tool p95 latency, recovery rate, and the added response token count. The token overhead of the enriched contract is MEASURED from the replay; any projected capacity effect derived from it is an ESTIMATE until read from serving counters.

Controlled experiment. Two arms on one frozen checkpoint replaying the same logged window with identical seeds, differing only in the response schema. Verify first that the numeric values are byte-identical across arms so the manipulation is purely the contract, then read the difference in unnecessary-call rate against a control-versus-control band. Stratify by whether the original result was rounded, since the mechanism predicts the effect concentrates there.

Confounders. The enriched response is longer, so prompt length and prefix cache behaviour shift alongside the semantic change; a length-matched arm carrying uninformative padding separates the two. A declared precision that is wrong is worse than none, because it licenses false confidence, so the precision field must be derived from the tool implementation rather than asserted. Some clients parse the response positionally and will break on schema change.

Rollback criteria. Revert the schema if any downstream consumer's parse-failure rate rises above zero, or if tool-required-stratum accuracy declines. The response schema must be versioned, with the prior version served in parallel during rollout so revert is a routing change rather than a redeploy, and the parallel window must be long enough to cover the slowest consumer's release cycle.
risks: Source answer treats repeated calling as a policy defect without examining whether the tool response is interpretable.
A declared precision that is wrong is worse than none because it licenses false confidence.
Downstream consumers that parse the response positionally break on any schema change.
evidence_required: Byte-identity check of numeric values across the bare and enriched response arms, establishing that only the contract changed.
Unnecessary-call rate stratified by whether the original result was rounded, plus a length-matched padding arm and downstream parse-failure counts.

STANCE 86 - Attribute the disposition to a training stage before choosing a fix: base, supervised and preference checkpoints can be measured separately, and the wrong stage cannot be repaired by the right technique.

Mechanism. A policy's tendency to re-call a tool is inherited from pretraining, shaped by supervised demonstrations and then reweighted by preference optimisation. Each stage leaves a distinguishable signature, and the lineage is available because the intermediate checkpoints exist. Choosing an intervention without locating the stage means, for example, editing prompts to fight a preference-stage equilibrium, which will be reverted by the next preference run.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: unnecessary-call rate differs across the base, supervised and preference checkpoints by more than the noise band, isolating at least one stage as the dominant contributor. Falsified if all three checkpoints show the same rate within the band, which would place the cause outside the training pipeline, in the prompt, tool schema or decode configuration.

Metrics. Unnecessary-call rate per checkpoint in the lineage, evaluated on one frozen eval set with identical decode configuration and seeds; share of supervised demonstrations that themselves contain a redundant call; tool-required-stratum accuracy per checkpoint; stop/no-tool eval score per checkpoint; trajectory length; and recovery rate. Every rate carries its checkpoint hash, and any figure quoted without the hash is treated as an ESTIMATE of unknown lineage.

Controlled experiment. Evaluate the lineage in one pass on the same items, holding the prompt, tool schema and decode configuration fixed so the only varying factor is the checkpoint. Independently, count redundant calls in the supervised training mixture itself with the same adjudication rule used for evaluation, since a demonstration-level base rate is a direct MEASURED cause rather than an inference. Where a stage is implicated, re-run that stage with the single hypothesised change and no other difference.

Confounders. Checkpoints in a lineage differ in more than one respect when data and hyperparameters moved together, so a stage-level difference is not automatically attributable to the stage's objective. Loss masking bugs make a demonstration count differ from what the model was actually trained on, so a decoded loss-mask audit is a precondition. Evaluation-set contamination differs across stages if the eval items entered any mixture.

Rollback criteria. Do not fund a weight-level fix unless the lineage measurement implicates a training stage and the demonstration base rate corroborates it. If a retrained stage regresses tool-required-stratum accuracy or recovery rate, revert to the prior checkpoint, which requires that the prior checkpoint remain retained and loadable for the full evaluation window rather than being garbage collected on a storage policy.
risks: Source answer proposes preference or reward signals without first locating which training stage produced the disposition.
Checkpoints in a lineage differ in data and hyperparameters together, so a stage difference is not automatically attributable to that stage's objective.
Loss-masking defects make the demonstration count differ from what the model was actually trained on.
evidence_required: Unnecessary-call rate per lineage checkpoint on one frozen eval set with prompt, tool schema, decode configuration and seeds held fixed.
Redundant-call base rate counted directly in the supervised training mixture under the same adjudication rule, preceded by a decoded loss-mask audit.

STANCE 87 - Derive the capacity claim from a queueing model with measured service times, because a count of removed calls does not by itself predict any change in served throughput.

Mechanism. Removing calls reduces offered work, but the resulting change in latency and throughput depends on where the system sits on its utilisation curve. Near saturation a small reduction in service demand produces a large drop in queueing delay; far from saturation it produces almost none. A claim that removing calls will improve p95 latency is therefore a statement about the operating point, and it must be derived from measured service times, arrival rates and concurrency rather than from the call count alone.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: the observed p95 latency change after a redundancy reduction matches the queueing-model prediction derived from measured service times and arrival rate within a pre-declared tolerance. Falsified if the observed change departs from the prediction beyond that tolerance, which would mean the model is missing a dominant term such as admission control or cache effects and no capacity claim may be made from it.

Metrics. Measured per-phase service times, arrival rate, concurrency, utilisation, queue depth and p95 end-to-end latency before and after, alongside the model's predicted latency change. Behavioural set as usual: unnecessary-call rate, tool success, tool-required-stratum accuracy, trajectory length, tool latency and recovery rate. Service times and arrival rates are MEASURED; the predicted latency change is an ESTIMATE and must be published before the after-measurement is taken.

Controlled experiment. Fit the model on a window with no intervention, pre-register its prediction for the intervention window, then measure. Sweep offered load in the replay to locate the utilisation region where the prediction is sensitive, rather than testing at a single operating point where any model would appear adequate. Establish a control-versus-control band first so a prediction error is distinguishable from run-to-run variance.

Confounders. Continuous batching makes per-request service time depend on batch composition, so service time is not a fixed parameter and must be reported as a distribution. Admission control and preemption introduce a control loop the simple model omits. Prefix cache hit rate changes with traffic mix and shifts prefill service time independently of the intervention.

Rollback criteria. Withdraw any capacity or cost claim whose prediction was falsified, and do not resize pools on a falsified model. Pool size changes made under a validated model must be revertible to the recorded prior values, and the revert must be exercised in staging before production application.
risks: Source answer treats removed call count as if it directly implied a latency or throughput improvement.
Continuous batching makes per-request service time depend on batch composition, so it is a distribution rather than a parameter.
Admission control and preemption introduce a control loop that a simple queueing model omits.
evidence_required: Measured per-phase service-time distributions, arrival rate, concurrency and utilisation from an unintervened window.
Pre-registered queueing-model latency prediction published before the after-measurement, with a load sweep locating the sensitive utilisation region.

STANCE 88 - Score the harm in context budget rather than currency: the operational failure from redundant observations is truncation of earlier necessary content, not the marginal cost of tokens.

Mechanism. Each retained tool observation occupies part of a fixed context window. In long trajectories the window is the binding constraint, and the eviction or truncation policy drops the oldest content first. Redundant observations therefore push out the task statement, constraints and earlier necessary results, producing wrong answers rather than merely expensive ones. Framing the defect as cost hides its most severe consequence and leads to interventions optimised for the wrong outcome.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: trajectories that exceed a context-occupancy threshold show a materially higher rate of dropping necessary earlier content, and their final-answer correctness is lower than length-matched trajectories below the threshold. Falsified if correctness is flat across occupancy strata, which would mean the window is not binding in this traffic and the cost framing is adequate.

Metrics. Context occupancy at each decision point, truncation events with the identity of the evicted span, rate of trajectories in which the task statement or a necessary earlier result was evicted, final correctness stratified by occupancy, unnecessary-call rate, tool success, tool-required-stratum accuracy, trajectory length, and recovery rate. Occupancy and truncation counts are MEASURED from the rendered prompt; any projected correctness gain from freeing the window is an ESTIMATE until the arm is run.

Controlled experiment. Instrument the renderer to log occupancy and eviction identity per turn, then compare correctness across occupancy strata on logged traffic. Follow with a two-arm replay in which the only change is summarising or dropping duplicate observations, holding the window size, eviction policy and decode configuration fixed, and check whether the eviction rate of necessary spans falls.

Confounders. Occupancy correlates with task difficulty, so high-occupancy trajectories are harder for reasons unrelated to eviction; length-matched comparison and difficulty stratification are required. Summarising an observation is lossy and can itself remove the necessary content, converting an eviction failure into a compression failure. Different serving builds apply different truncation policies, so the policy version must be pinned.

Rollback criteria. Revert the deduplication or summarisation change if final correctness on long trajectories declines, or if any necessary-span eviction rate rises. Because this is a prompt-assembly change in the serving path, the prior assembler must remain available behind a flag and the revert must be exercised in staging before rollout.
risks: Source answer frames the defect as cost and omits the context-window budget that binds in long trajectories.
Occupancy correlates with task difficulty, so high-occupancy trajectories are harder for unrelated reasons.
Summarising an observation is lossy and can convert an eviction failure into a compression failure.
evidence_required: Per-turn context occupancy and truncation events with the identity of the evicted span, logged by the prompt renderer.
Final correctness stratified by occupancy against length-matched and difficulty-stratified comparators, with the truncation policy version pinned.

STANCE 89 - Randomise item order and rotate adjudicators, because a replay evaluated in fixed order measures cache warmth and labeller drift alongside the intervention.

Mechanism. A replay that presents items in the same order to every arm gives later items a warmer prefix cache and gives human adjudicators a fatigue gradient that correlates with position. Both effects are position-dependent and therefore confounded with anything else that varies along the sequence. Because the arms share infrastructure, the confound does not cancel; it accumulates in whichever arm runs later or is labelled later.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: re-running the identical arm with a different item order changes the measured unnecessary-call rate by more than the control-versus-control noise band established at fixed order. Falsified if order permutation leaves the rate inside that band, which would license fixed-order replay for this harness and eliminate a class of confound.

Metrics. Unnecessary-call rate per arm under at least two independent item orders, prefix cache hit rate by item position, adjudicator agreement by position within a labelling session, labelling throughput by position, and the standard behavioural set of tool success, tool-required-stratum accuracy, trajectory length, tool latency and recovery rate. The order-permutation spread is MEASURED and becomes the floor beneath which no effect may be claimed.

Controlled experiment. Run each arm under two pre-declared item orders generated from recorded seeds, interleave the arms rather than running them sequentially, and assign adjudicators to items by a randomised schedule that balances position across labellers. Compare the between-order spread against the between-arm difference before interpreting the latter.

Confounders. Randomising order changes cache behaviour in a way that can itself alter latency-sensitive behaviour, so latency metrics must be read per order rather than pooled. Adjudicator rotation introduces between-labeller variance in place of within-labeller drift, which is preferable but must be measured with duplicate labelling. Some harnesses cache by item identity, so a permutation does not clear the cache and the check silently passes.

Rollback criteria. This is a measurement gate: refuse to report any effect smaller than the measured order-permutation spread, and re-run at adequate scale instead. If a previously reported result did not control order, restate it as provisional and re-measure under randomised order before it is used to justify a rollout.
risks: Source answer specifies a controlled experiment without controlling item order or adjudicator assignment.
Shared harness infrastructure means position-dependent cache warmth does not cancel between arms.
Harnesses that cache by item identity are unaffected by permutation, so the order check can silently pass.
evidence_required: Unnecessary-call rate for each arm under at least two pre-declared item orders generated from recorded seeds.
Adjudicator agreement and throughput by position within a session under a randomised assignment schedule, with duplicate labelling.

STANCE 90 - Version and pin the tool itself: the calculator is a dependency that changes, and a result cached or labelled under one version is not valid under the next.

Mechanism. The tool has its own release cycle. Rounding behaviour, precision, error semantics and even numeric results can change between versions. Any mechanism that reuses a prior result, whether an in-context observation, a memoisation cache or a historical adjudication label, implicitly assumes the tool is stable. When the tool changes underneath, the reuse becomes a correctness defect and the historical labels become invalid, yet neither failure announces itself.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: at least one tool version change within the analysis window alters the result for a non-empty set of replayed argument tuples, invalidating reuse and historical labels for that set. Falsified if replaying every logged argument tuple against every version in the window produces byte-identical results, which would license cross-version reuse and pooling for this window.

Metrics. Tool version stamped on every call record, count of argument tuples whose result differs across versions, share of cached or reused results affected, share of historical adjudication labels invalidated, and the standard behavioural set of tool success, tool-required-stratum accuracy, trajectory length, tool p95 latency and recovery rate. The cross-version result diff is MEASURED by replaying the tool alone and requires no model inference.

Controlled experiment. Replay the recorded argument tuples against each tool version present in the window and diff the outputs; this isolates tool drift from policy behaviour entirely. Where differences exist, recompute the affected metrics with those items excluded and report both figures. Before enabling any memoisation, require the cache key to include the tool version and demonstrate in passive mode that live and cached results agree byte-for-byte within a version.

Confounders. Non-deterministic tools, for example those consulting a live data source, produce diffs that are not version drift and must be separated by a same-version repeat call. Version strings that do not change on behavioural change make the stamp useless, so the stamp must be derived from the deployed artifact rather than declared. Client-side formatting can mask an underlying difference.

Rollback criteria. Invalidate and purge every cache entry whose key lacks a tool version, and treat any adjudication label produced before a behaviour-changing version as unusable rather than adjusted. If a memoisation layer is already live without version-keyed entries, disable it by a single flag before further analysis, and re-enable only after the passive-mode agreement audit passes on the current version.
risks: Source answer treats the tool as a fixed oracle whose results are comparable across the analysis window.
Memoisation and in-context reuse become correctness defects when the tool changes underneath them.
Version strings that do not change on behavioural change make the version stamp useless.
evidence_required: Cross-version replay of recorded argument tuples against every tool version in the window, diffed without model inference.
Passive-mode byte-for-byte agreement audit between live and cached results within a single version, with the version stamp derived from the deployed artifact.
